prompt.context: Our client, DigiBooks, is a manufacturer and seller of electronic book readers (tablets). DigiBooks also distributes e-books for the tablets through their website. The tablet is only compatible with books sold through the DigiBooks site. DigiBooks is planning the launch of its tablets in a country where no electronic book readers are currently sold. Only 1% of the population has ever used an electronic book reader, though 50% is aware of the concept. The country has a total population of 76 million and a high literacy level. No competitors in the e-book or tablet space plan to enter this country. DigiBooks has never sold a product outside of the US. The DigiBooks tablet uses an e-ink electronic paper display featuring 16 shades of grey, allowing for a 12-hour battery life and easy readability.
prompt.question: The Chief Marketing Officer of DigiBooks has come to you to help determine: How should DigiBooks launch and market DigiBook tablets in this new country?

clarifying_info.q: What is an electronic book reader?
clarifying_info.a: A software, hardware and network platform that utilizes wireless connectivity to enable users to shop for, download, browse, and read e-books, newspapers, magazines, blogs, and other digital media.

clarifying_info.q: Are there competitors planning to enter this market?
clarifying_info.a: No competitors in the e-book or tablet space plan to enter this country.
DigiBooks has never sold a product outside of the US.

clarifying_info.q: What is the total population of the country?
clarifying_info.a: 76 million, with a high literacy level.

exhibits.title: Market Segments
exhibits.shows: A table listing three customer segments with their respective population sizes and suggested e-reader price points.
exhibits.data: Super Readers (SR): 8M people, tablet price $200; Occasional Readers (OR): 20M people, tablet price $125; Rare Readers (RR): 10M people, tablet price $175

exhibits.title: Channel Decisions
exhibits.shows: A table comparing two sales channels (Retail and Internet) across four metrics: reach as a percentage of total potential market, e-book gross margin %, e-reader gross margin %, penetration rate, and overhead costs.
exhibits.data: Retail: Reach 50%, E-book GM 50%, E-reader GM 30%, Penetration 40%, Overheads $20M; Internet: Reach 50%, E-book GM 50%, E-reader GM 60%, Penetration 10%, Overheads $10M

framework: Segmentation, Targeting & Positioning: Identify which customer segments exist, evaluate size and attractiveness, and select the most valuable segment to target
Product: Assess whether existing tablet product meets the needs of the target country or requires adaptation for this new market
Price: Determine appropriate price points for both the tablet hardware and e-books; consider razor-and-blade pricing model (low tablet price, margin on e-books)
Promotion: Identify marketing and advertising mechanisms best suited to reach the target segment in this country
Place / Distribution: Evaluate retail vs. internet vs. other distribution channels for selling and delivering the tablets
Selection of e-books: Assess whether a sufficient catalog of e-books in the relevant language(s) is available for this country

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1 and a 3-year revenue projection, which customer segment should DigiBooks target? (Note: e-book price is $10 per book; assume all tablet sales happen immediately and ignore time value of money.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate 3-year revenue potential for each segment by combining tablet revenue and e-book revenue over three years, then compare totals. Missing data to request: average e-book price ($10). Occasional Readers yields the highest revenue potential at $8.5B despite having a lower per-capita spend than Super Readers, due to the much larger segment size (20M vs 8M).

math.setup: Revenue per segment = (Books/year x $10/book x 3 years + Tablet price) x Segment size
steps: SR Revenue = (15 books x $10 x 3 years + $200 tablet) x 8M = ($450 + $200) x 8M = $650 x 8M = $5.2B
OR Revenue = (10 books x $10 x 3 years + $125 tablet) x 20M = ($300 + $125) x 20M = $425 x 20M = $8.5B
RR Revenue = (5 books x $10 x 3 years + $175 tablet) x 10M = ($150 + $175) x 10M = $325 x 10M = $3.25B
math.answer: Target Occasional Readers (OR) with a 3-year revenue potential of $8.5B — the highest of the three segments.

questions.prompt: DigiBooks is now considering whether to sell its e-book readers through retail stores or through the internet. How would you go about evaluating this decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure a qualitative pros/cons comparison. Strong answers cover: Retail pros — encourages product trial, enables joint marketing with retailers, retailers handle customer service and returns; Retail cons — lower margin due to additional value chain participants, time and cost to establish, training costs. Internet pros — likely cheaper to establish, higher gross margins; Internet cons — harder to encourage trial of a new/unfamiliar product. No quantitative data required for this prompt.

questions.prompt: Based on revised market estimates, DigiBooks has decided to price the e-reader at $100 and target the Occasional Reader segment (20M people). Using Exhibit 2, estimate the 1-year profit potential of each sales channel. Which channel should DigiBooks choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate annual profit for each channel using Exhibit 2 data. The potential market is the OR segment (20M people). Revenue comes from two streams: e-book sales (10 books/year x $10/book) and tablet hardware ($100/tablet). Apply the respective gross margins and penetration/reach rates, then subtract overhead. Retail wins on absolute profit despite lower e-reader margin, because its penetration rate (40%) is four times that of Internet (10%).

math.setup: Channel Profit = [(10 books x $10/book x E-book GM%) + ($100/tablet x E-reader GM%)] x (20M people x Reach% x Penetration%) - Overheads
math.answer: Retail channel profit = $300M; Internet channel profit = $100M. Choose Retail.

recommendation: DigiBooks should launch the e-book reader targeting the Occasional Reader segment (20M people) through the Retail sales channel
This strategy is projected to generate approximately $300M in annual profit after $20M in overhead costs
risks: Future competitor entry could erode market share and margins
Establishing a retail distribution network in a new country takes time and upfront investment
Insufficient e-book catalog in the local language could limit adoption
Manufacturing and logistics costs for an international market have not been assessed
next_steps: Determine advertising and promotional mechanisms appropriate for this country
Decide whether to set up local manufacturing or source from existing US facilities
Assess the breadth of local-language e-book catalog available for the DigiBooks platform
Monitor for any competitor announcements to enter the market
